asha: Quick heads-up: bring-up for reranker-v2a (FP16 -> PTQ int8) is failing smoke: -0.035 NDCG@10 and -0.018 MRR@10 vs FP16 on the standard smoke holdout. No obvious model-change other than preprocessing tweaks.

dan: Which preprocessing tweaks? any token ids changed?

asha: We swapped the doc concatenation delimiter in the new ingest to `[SEP]` (literal text) instead of two newlines. Also the template priming now inserts a 128-token `__PRIME_PAD__` region for multi-turn alignment. Eval command: `./tools/eval_runner.py --model rerank-v2a-int8 --holdout smoke-50k --k 10 --seed 1234`. Logs: https://artifacts.redwood/rs/378901 (summary csv attached there).

kevin: Two quick experiments to run: 1) restore old delimiter and run the same eval, 2) strip priming pad tokens before tokenization and rerun. Also produce a tokenizer token-count diff between FP16 baseline and v2a preprocessing.

asha: On it. Running variants now: baseline (A), restore-delim (B), strip-prime (C), and combined (D). Will also run `python -m tools.token_count_diff --a=baseline.jsonl --b=v2a.jsonl` to get seqlen delta.

eval-bot: Job queued: eval-job-99112 (variants A-D). Artifacts: https://console.redwood/jobs/99112. ETA ~22m.

dan: FYI if the seqlen distribution shifts right, PTQ tends to show larger relative error since KV cache and attention scale interact with quant ranges. Keep an eye on mean and 95th pct.

asha: Results in. Quick summary: B (restore-delim) recovered +0.026 NDCG@10 and +0.013 MRR@10 vs A. C (strip-prime) recovered +0.009 NDCG and +0.006 MRR. D (both) recovered +0.035 NDCG and +0.020 MRR, effectively eliminating the regression (~+0.001 delta vs FP16). Token-count diff shows mean tokens per input up ~6% with v2a preprocessing (priming pad contributes most). 95th pct up 12%.

kevin: That strongly smells like formatting-induced distribution shift rather than PTQ math error. Two actions: 1) add a formatting parity step to the bringup smoke (force old delimiter + strip prime by default) so quant config isn't signed off with perturbed inputs; 2) add a seqlen monitor in the quant pipeline to alert if mean/95th change > 5% from baseline.

dan: Agreed. Also add a short test in the eval harness: when a quant model is promoted, run a small diff where you feed the FP16 and INT8 runs the same normalized-text pipeline and assert NDCG delta <= 0.01 on smoke holdout. That catches regressions caused by incidental preprocessing changes.

asha: Filed INF-2410: "rerank-v2a bringup: formatting parity + seqlen guardrails". Included commands to reproduce and the minimal normalizer script I used: 
```
# tiny normalizer used in B/C/D variants
import sys, json
for line in sys.stdin:
    r = json.loads(line)
    text = r['doc_text'].replace('[SEP]', '\\n\\n')
    text = ' '.join(text.split())
    r['doc_text_norm'] = text
    print(json.dumps(r))
```

kevin: Nice. One more: add a note to the model card and onboarding doc that any change to concat delimiter or priming pads must trigger a re-eval and explicit sign-off for quantized variants. We've had this slip through before.

dan: Also let's capture a small CSV of per-query deltas (ndcg_fp16, ndcg_int8) for the smoke set and save it to the job artifacts so future triage is faster.

eval-bot: Artifacts updated: https://console.redwood/jobs/99112/artifacts. Per-query-deltas.csv uploaded.

asha: Thanks all — I'll push the preproc parity patch to the bringup branch and re-run the full PTQ flow. Will post final sign-off here once clean.

kevin: Great, and thanks for including the tiny normalizer snippet. Saves time for anyone reproducing the issue.

asha: Marking thread as the canonical repro thread and closing once sign-off is posted. Ping me for raw CSV if you want per-slice analyses. :white_check_mark:
